Documentation → Monitoring & Analysis → Service checks

Service checks — is the service really working?

Prove that a web page, an SSL VPN, OpenVPN, IPsec or WireGuard endpoint, or a TLS, DNS, SSH, SMTP or TCP service answers at its own protocol level — with the certificate it presents, a screenshot for web pages, uptime, history and alerts.

👤 ForOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsobservability.access monitoring.view monitoring.probe_free
📍 WhereObservability › Monitoring → Service checks (every ADOM) (URL /observability/monitoring/checks/)

What is it?#

Service checks answer does the service really work? — not is its port open. A port can accept connections while the service behind it is broken, so each check speaks the service's own protocol and judges the answer: a web page must return the expected status and content, an OpenVPN server must answer an OpenVPN handshake, an IPsec gateway an IKE exchange, a WireGuard server a WireGuard handshake. Where the protocol shows a certificate, the check reads it too.

The page has three tabs — Web, VPN and Ports & protocols — tiles with how many checks are up, degraded, down or not run yet, and a detail view per check with its certificate, the protocol facts of the last run, a strip of recent results and the last 24 hours.

What does it do?#

Tab Service Up means Certificate
Web HTTPS website the URL answers an expected status (default 200-399) after at most 5 redirects, and contains the keyword if you set one; a screenshot is kept subject, issuer, names, validity, days left, chain trusted, name matches
Web HTTP website the same, without TLS —
VPN SSL VPN TLS handshake, then the vendor's login portal answers with its own page (Fortinet /remote/login; Cisco, Palo Alto, Pulse, or generic) the portal's
VPN OpenVPN a real OpenVPN reset handshake over UDP or TCP — with the server's tls-auth or tls-crypt key when it uses one the server's, read through the control channel (TLS 1.2)
VPN IPsec (IKE) the responder answers an IKE_SA_INIT (IKEv2, or IKEv1 Main Mode; NAT-T on UDP 4500 optional). Any IKE reply — even no proposal chosen — proves the daemon. Optionally name a managed FortiGate and the tunnel: its monitor API then says whether the tunnel's phase-2 selectors are up none — IKE sends certificates only inside its encrypted exchange
VPN WireGuard a real WireGuard handshake whose response authenticates with the expected keys none — WireGuard uses static keys
Ports & protocols TLS · DNS · SSH · SMTP · TCP a TLS handshake · an answer record · the SSH identification line · the SMTP banner (and STARTTLS) · a connection, or a banner you describe TLS and SMTP

Each run ends in one status:

  • Up — the service answered correctly.
  • Degraded — it answered, but something soft is wrong: a certificate within the warning period (default 21 days), or an untrusted certificate you chose to accept.
  • Down — no answer, the wrong answer, a missing keyword, an unexpected HTTP status, an expired certificate, or an untrusted one when trust is required.
  • Error — SATOM refused the destination or the check is misconfigured.

How to use#

  1. 1Add checkPick the service and fill its fields (URL, host and port, keys…)
  2. 2Save and runThe check runs once at once, with a screenshot for web pages
  3. 3WatchThe monitor sweep runs it again whenever its interval has elapsed
  4. 4DetailCertificate, protocol facts, last results, screenshot
  1. Open Observability › Monitoring → Service checks and press Add check.
  2. Pick the Service. The form shows only that service's fields, with a one-line note on what "up" means for it.
  3. Choose how often (Every, 3 minutes to 24 hours), the Timeout, the Certificate warning days and, for web pages and SSL VPN, Screenshot every (minutes; 0 = never).
  4. Save and run. The check runs immediately; open it (card or list icon) to see the result.

WireGuard: add the monitoring peer#

WireGuard answers only keys it knows — that silence is its design. Press Generate to create a key pair for the monitoring peer, then add the shown public key as a peer on the WireGuard server (an unused /32 as AllowedIPs is enough). Fill in the server's public key and save. Until the peer exists the check stays down, and says why.

OpenVPN: tls-auth and tls-crypt#

A server that uses tls-auth or tls-crypt drops every packet without the right HMAC. Paste the static key (the -----BEGIN OpenVPN Static key V1----- block) and, for tls-auth, the key direction the clients use. Without it the check reports down and suggests supplying the key.

IPsec: the tunnel itself#

The IKE probe proves the gateway's IKE service answers from where SATOM is. To know whether a given tunnel is up, pick a managed FortiGate and type the tunnel's phase-1 name: SATOM reads the tunnel table (read only) and the check goes down when no phase-2 selector of that tunnel is up.

Screenshots#

Web pages and SSL VPN portals get a 1366×768 screenshot when the check is saved and then at most every Screenshot every minutes. The browser is the node's Chromium, run headless inside a bubblewrap sandbox: read-only system, private temporary files, only the output folder writable. The last five pictures per check are kept. A node without Chromium says so on the page and takes none — add the distribution's chromium package (EPEL on RHEL); the online installer tries it for you.

When checks run#

With the deep_monitor scheduled action, every 3 minutes — nothing new to arm. A check runs when its interval has elapsed (intervals are multiples of 3 minutes), and again whenever you save it or press ▶. The last 2,000 results per check are kept, none older than 90 days.

Alerts#

A check that is down raises a critical alert and a degraded one a warning, through Settings → Email & Alerts (the device checks family). The bell icon on a check mutes its alerts; it keeps running and recording. Pause stops it running.

Permissions and safety#

  • Reading the page needs observability.access and monitoring.view.
  • Adding, editing, running, muting, pausing and deleting need a configuration-write permission and monitoring.probe_free (or user management) — the same rule as the certificate inspector and the transaction tracer, because a check dials a host of your choosing from the management network. Every change, run and refusal is in the audit log (service_check.*).
  • Every destination, on save and before every connection of every run, passes the same guard: cloud instance-metadata addresses are never dialled, and the SSH and mail ports are allowed only to the checks that speak SSH or SMTP.
  • Keys are secrets. OpenVPN static keys and WireGuard private and preshared keys are stored in the vault, or encrypted in the settings, never in the check itself, and never shown again. Leave the field empty when editing to keep the stored key.
  • Checks belong to the ADOM they were created in; the Global ADOM shows them all.

Troubleshooting#

Symptom Cause and fix
A WireGuard check stays down with "no handshake response" WireGuard answers only peers it knows. Add the monitoring peer's public key (shown when you pressed Generate) as a peer on the server, then Run now.
An OpenVPN check is down and suggests a key The server uses tls-auth or tls-crypt and drops packets without the right HMAC. Paste the static key (and, for tls-auth, the key direction the clients use).
An IPsec check is down with "no IKE response" Nothing answers IKE on that address and port from SATOM's network: check the gateway listens on UDP 500 (or 4500 with NAT-T) and that a firewall lets SATOM through.
An IPsec check is up but the tunnel is broken The IKE probe proves the daemon, not a tunnel. Name the managed FortiGate and the phase-1 name to read the tunnel itself.
A web check is degraded with "certificate does not match the host name" The URL's host is not in the certificate's names. Use the name the certificate carries, or accept it on purpose (untick Require a trusted certificate).
"Screenshots are off on this node" The node has no Chromium (or no bubblewrap). Add the distribution's chromium package; the next run takes the picture.
A screenshot never comes back and the run says the page did not finish rendering The page is not reachable from SATOM's node within the timeout (a name that resolves to an address SATOM cannot reach, for example). Check from the node itself.
Saving fails with "SATOM refuses …" The destination is refused by the network guard: a cloud metadata address, an internal port of the node, or an SSH/SMTP port for a check that does not speak SSH/SMTP.
Add check is missing You need a configuration-write permission and <a class="dc-perm" href="permissions.html#monitoring-probe_free" title="Probe free targets — Point the certificate inspector and the transaction tracer at a
host SATOM does not manage. Inventory destinations never need this.">monitoring.probe_free.
